note: Verified facts for the showcase series (Kenya at its best, Built in Kenya). Each `fact` is taken from the page in `source`, checked by hand on 18 Oct 2026. The writer may only use the fact given; it writes the words around it. Add entries the same way: one fact, quoted from an official or newsroom page, under 150 characters.

entries.name: Hell's Gate National Park
entries.fact: Gazetted in 1984, the park covers about 68 square kilometres of cliffs, gorges and geothermal steam on the Rift Valley floor.

entries.name: Nairobi National Park
entries.fact: Gazetted in 1946 as Kenya's first national park, it covers 117 square kilometres just outside the city.
entries.photo_query: Nairobi National Park skyline giraffe Kenya

entries.name: Aberdare National Park
entries.fact: Its Mau Mau Post Office tree, a mugumo fig, was a secret message drop for Mau Mau fighters.

entries.name: Lake Nakuru National Park
entries.fact: The park covers about 188 square kilometres and is fenced as a sanctuary for black and white rhinos.
entries.photo_query: Lake Nakuru National Park flamingos Kenya

entries.name: Mount Kenya National Park
entries.fact: At 5,199 metres, Mount Kenya is the second highest peak in Africa, says UNESCO.

entries.name: Lamu Old Town
entries.fact: UNESCO calls Lamu the oldest and best-preserved Swahili town in East Africa, lived in for over 700 years.

entries.name: Fort Jesus
entries.fact: Built by the Portuguese in 1593-1596 to guard Mombasa's port, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

entries.name: Lake Turkana National Parks
entries.fact: UNESCO calls Turkana the most saline of Africa's large lakes; its Koobi Fora deposits are rich in fossils.

entries.name: Kenya Lake System
entries.fact: Up to 4 million lesser flamingos move between lakes Bogoria, Nakuru and Elementaita for most of the year, says UNESCO.

entries.name: Thimlich Ohinga
entries.fact: Built in the 16th century, these dry-stone fortified settlements became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2018.

entries.name: Nairobi Expressway
entries.fact: The 27.1-kilometre road runs from Mlolongo to the James Gichuru junction on Waiyaki Way and opened on 14 May 2022.

entries.name: Madaraka Express (SGR)
entries.fact: The standard gauge railway runs 472 kilometres from Mombasa to Nairobi; the Madaraka Express began on 31 May 2017.

entries.name: Lake Turkana Wind Power
entries.fact: Its 365 turbines in Loiyangalani, Marsabit County, can produce 310 megawatts.
entries.photo_query: Lake Turkana Wind Power turbines Kenya

entries.name: Garissa Solar Power Plant
entries.fact: With 54.65 megawatts installed, REREC calls it the largest grid-connected solar plant in East and Central Africa.

entries.name: Lamu Port
entries.fact: Lamu Port's first berth opened in May 2021; when complete the port will have 32 berths.

entries.name: Thika Superhighway
entries.fact: The eight-lane road runs about 50 kilometres from Nairobi to Thika and was launched in November 2012.

entries.name: Olkaria geothermal plants
entries.fact: KenGen had 713 megawatts of geothermal capacity at Olkaria, Naivasha, in 2022: power from the earth's heat.
